headline: High-risk interaction: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP can leak or misapply outputs, while spring-integration-samples adds no documented safeguards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can ingest and emit via browsers, subprocesses, and MCP, so attacker-controlled content could be routed into its tool chain. spring-integration-samples has no documented runtime surfaces, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than observed. The pathway exists if outputs are copied through shared files or MCP, but the second agent’s lack of runtime detail prevents a higher severity.
conditions: IF LightAgent reads untrusted web or MCP content as instructions
IF the two agents exchange content through a shared file, clipboard, or MCP bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content
Route inter-agent text through a human review step
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add provenance tags to all MCP payloads
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, and it has broad network egress. spring-integration-samples is documented as network-egress none, so the main leakage risk is one-way from LightAgent if sensitive data is forwarded into its outputs or APIs. The pair lacks documented shared storage, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards conversation or memory content into external APIs
IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace or transcript
mitigations: Remove secrets from LightAgent prompts
Keep separate directories for each agent
Turn off unnecessary logging in LightAgent
Review outbound API destinations before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the egress boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and supports multiple instances, which can create local write contention if it shares mutable state. spring-integration-samples is not runnable and exposes no write or concurrency surface in the profile, so there is no documented overlapping mutable resource. The conflict pathway is therefore limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same local files or workflow state
IF LightAgent instances run concurrently against one mutable workspace
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one LightAgent instance per workspace
Lock shared files before writes
Make spring-integration-samples read-only
requires-engineering: add advisory file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool calls, tool results, and workflow state that another system may treat as authoritative. spring-integration-samples is a docs/sample repository, so it is unlikely to act autonomously, but if its outputs are wired into a downstream workflow the pair can cascade errors without verification. Uncertainty about the second agent’s runtime behavior keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF LightAgent output is consumed as authoritative by a downstream workflow
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped in an automation that executes generated instructions
mitigations: Require human approval before acting on outputs
Add a verification step between agents
Log and diff intermediate artifacts
Limit LightAgent to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles user conversations and long-term memory, which can create retention or residency obligations. spring-integration-samples has no documented data classes or residency controls, so there is no direct pairwise compliance mismatch evidenced here. The risk is limited to unusual deployment choices that route regulated data through LightAgent.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into LightAgent
IF the deployment stores conversations or memory beyond the required retention period
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to LightAgent
Set short retention on logs and memory
Document data handling responsibilities
Review secret-handling settings before launch
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
